name: multi_entity
description: B38 Phase 0 follow-up: 10 questions that each need TWO AIDLC knowledge-base entries. Tests where graph-aware retrieval (neo4j_graph_rerank) might beat plain vector search; split by whether the pair is declared RELATED_TO in the B37 graph.
_comment: B38 (2026-11-12). The golden set's conceptual half is 9 single-concept lookups and 1 comparison question; on it,
graph rerank LOST on average (context relevancy 0.948 -> 0.860) but WON on the one comparison question
(ADKAR vs Kotter, 0.867 -> 0.967) by pulling in the second framework vector search missed. This set tests that
signal with ten such questions, each naming two entries that exist in the knowledge base (verified in Neo4j).
TWO HALVES, deliberately, so the graph is not only graded on cases built for it:
multi-linked   (6) - the two entries ARE declared (:Entry)-[:RELATED_TO]-(:Entry): event-storming /
jobs-to-be-done-research / kano-model, tech-radar / wardley-mapping, concept-drift / data-drift.
multi-unlinked (4) - the two entries share tags but have NO RELATED_TO edge: kafka / spark, llm-caching /
retrieval-augmented-generation. The graph cannot connect these, so it should not help here.
Pinned like golden.json: editing it changes the exam. Run it with run config question_set: multi_entity.

questions.q: How do Event Storming and Service Blueprinting differ in what they map, and when would you use each?
How can stakeholder mapping and a RACI matrix be used together when planning a change?
What is the difference between MoSCoW prioritization and RICE scoring?
How do Jobs-to-be-Done research and the Kano model complement each other in product discovery?
How does a Tech Radar differ from a Wardley Map as a tool for technology strategy?
What is the difference between concept drift and data drift in a machine learning system?
When would you use Kafka versus Spark in a data platform?
How do LLM caching and the choice between online and batch inference each affect serving cost and latency?
How do a Git workflow and automated code formatting and linting work together to keep a codebase consistent?
How does a feature store differ from the retrieval layer of a retrieval-augmented generation system?
